verification_entries.claim: SIMD code paths exist and have scalar fallbacks
verification_entries.finding: simd_streaming_dfg.rs:137-174,231-261 uses std::arch::wasm32 v128 intrinsics, cfg-gated to target_arch=wasm32, with an explicit scalar fallback for other targets. simd_inner_loops.rs has x86 target_feature-gated tiers (avx512f/avx2/sse4.2) with scalar fallback -- these tiers do not actually use vector intrinsics (scalar loops behind cfg guards), so they are bit-identical to scalar by construction, not merely tested-equivalent. lib.rs:14 declares #![feature(portable_simd)] (nightly) but no std::simd usage was found beyond the flag itself.

verification_entries.result: PASS -- 23/23 simd-prefixed tests pass (cargo test --lib simd), re-run this checkpoint, 0 failures.
verification_entries.scope_note: these compare SIMD-code-path vs scalar-code-path output within ONE compilation target -- not a cross-target (native vs wasm32) execution comparison.

ledger_entries.claim: native-vs-wasm32 cross-target execution output equivalence (running the SAME compiled algorithm on both a native target and an actual wasm32 runtime, diffing results)

evidence.native_side: cargo test --test wasm_equivalence_native -- runs discover_dfg_from_log and EventLog::event_count/case_count directly (pure Rust, no wasm-bindgen), writes wasm-equivalence-tests/native_output.json
evidence.wasm32_side: node wasm-equivalence-tests/compare.mjs -- loads the wasm-pack nodejs-target build (wasm4pm/wasm4pm/pkg, built via 'wasm-pack build --target nodejs --out-dir pkg'), executes discover_dfg and analyze_event_statistics under Node's real wasm32 (V8 WebAssembly) runtime against the SAME fixture_log.json, writes wasm_output.json, and deep-equality-diffs against native_output.json
evidence.result: AGREE -- byte-identical JSON (after JSON.parse of the wasm side's to_js_str string envelope) for both algorithms, on a 3-case/9-event/4-activity fixed fixture log with a repeated activity (B->B) and divergent start/end activities.
evidence.normalization_applied: wasm-side outputs are returned as JSON strings via to_js_str (src/discovery.rs:145, src/analysis.rs:64) specifically to avoid the to_js(&json!({...}))->{} divergence; the only normalization is JSON.parse() of that string on the JS side to obtain a comparable object graph. This does not alter field names, key order semantics, or numeric values -- it undoes the string envelope required to cross the wasm-bindgen boundary, and is documented in both compare.mjs and wasm_equivalence_native.rs.

known_divergences_already_documented: to_js(&json!({...})) returns {} on wasm32 -- must use to_js_str() instead (CLAUDE.md gotcha, confirmed still relevant; both algorithms chosen this checkpoint already use to_js_str, so this divergence did NOT affect them)

OcelLog field names differ on wasm32 (CLAUDE.md gotcha -- checkpoint 017's Explore agent found THREE distinct OcelLog types across crates, this refers specifically to bcinr_powl::ocel::OcelLog, not wasm4pm::models::OCEL; not exercised by DFG discovery or event statistics, so not applicable to this checkpoint's scope)

ActorId::as_bytes() fails on wasm32 -- use .public_key instead (CLAUDE.md gotcha, confirmed still relevant; not exercised by DFG discovery or event statistics, so not applicable to this checkpoint's scope)
ledger_entries.conclusion: For the 2 algorithms exercised this checkpoint (DFG discovery, event statistics), native and wasm32 execution produce identical output on a fixed, deterministic fixture. This does NOT establish equivalence for the full algorithm surface of the crate (dozens of discover_*/analyze_* functions exist) -- only these 2 were run through the new harness. The 3 known CLAUDE.md divergences remain unaddressed and, by design, were sidestepped rather than fixed by picking algorithms that already route through to_js_str and do not touch OcelLog or ActorId.
